# Set the color palette and graphics

```{r consistent color palette by treatment}
colorz <- moma.colors("Warhol", n=15, type="discrete")

b.color <- colorz[3]
control.color <- colorz[9]
crab.color <- colorz[1]
n.color <- colorz[6]
```

# Read in data

```{r}
physiology_1 <- read_csv(here("data", "physiology.csv"))
metadata <- read_csv(here("data", "metadata.csv"))
```

# Prepare data

Clean, join, and scale data

```{r}
metadata %>% 
  # join metadata and physiology data
  inner_join(physiology_1) %>% 
  # turn categories into indicators
  mutate(crab = case_when(
    crab == "Y" ~ 1,
    crab == "N" ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ -9999
    )) %>% 
  mutate(nutrients = case_when( 
    nutrients == "Y" ~ 1,
    nutrients == "N" ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ -9999
    )) %>% 
  mutate(interaction = nutrients*crab) %>% 
  # scale variables
  mutate(protein_change_scale = scale(protein_change)[,1],
         carb_change_scale = scale(carb_change)[,1],
         endosym_change_scale = scale(endosym_percent_change)[,1],
         dflav_density_scale = scale(dflav_density_per_1000cm3)[,1],
         gmono_density_scale = scale(gmono_density_per_1000cm3)[,1],
         sa_T1_scale = scale(sa_cm2_T1)[,1],
         sa_T3_scale = scale(sa_cm2_T3)[,1]
         ) -> scaled_data
```

# Make individual models

First we'll fit individual models. Most will be shared between protein and carb models

# Overall models

D. flavicaudus model

```{r D. flavicaudus model}
m.dflav <- lmer(dflav_density_scale ~ nutrients + (1|block),
                # REML = FALSE, # add if you want to calculate SEM chi-squared (but then won't work with summary())
                data = scaled_data) 
```

Note the `isSingular` message is because block is not improving the model/block effects are estimated near zero. We'll keep block anyway because of the design.

```{r check model}
check_model(m.dflav)
```

G. monodonta model

```{r G. monodonta model}
m.gmono <- lmer(gmono_density_scale ~ crab + (1|block),
                # REML = FALSE, # add if you want to calculate SEM chi-squared (but then won't work with summary())
                data = scaled_data)
```

Note the `isSingular` message is because block is not improving the model/block effects are estimated near zero. We'll keep block anyway because of the design.

```{r check model}
check_model(m.gmono)
  check_normality(simulate_residuals(m.gmono))
```

Endosymbiont density model

```{r endosymbiont model}
m.endo <- lmer(endosym_change_scale ~ nutrients + (1|block),
               # REML = FALSE, # add if you want to calculate SEM chi-squared (but then won't work with summary())
               data = scaled_data)
```

Note the `isSingular` message is because block is not improving the model/block effects are estimated near zero. We'll keep block anyway because of the design.

```{r check model}
check_model(m.endo)
```

# Protein model

```{r protein model}
m.prot.health <- lmer(protein_change_scale ~ nutrients + crab + interaction + 
                        endosym_change_scale + dflav_density_scale + gmono_density_scale + 
                        sa_T1_scale + sa_T3_scale + (1|block),
                      # REML = FALSE, # add if you want to calculate SEM chi-squared (but then won't work with summary())
                      data = scaled_data)
```

```{r check model}
check_model(m.prot.health)
```

Create pSEM

```{r pSEM}
sem.prot <- psem(
  m.dflav, 
  m.gmono, 
  m.endo, 
  m.prot.health,
  gmono_density_scale %~~% sa_T3_scale, # correlated error
  data = as.data.frame(scaled_data)
)
```

```{r summary}
summary(sem.prot, conserve = TRUE)

# for chi-squared (run on non-REML model):
# LLchisq(sem.prot) # same as without random effect
```

**Notes on the summary output:**
- For tests of directed separation, p-values > 0.05 means those paths are justified to exclude
- Fischer's C statistic > 0.05 provides support for the hypothesized model structure
- Do NOT report Chi-squared values for models fit with REML--if you want the chi-squared values (13.132 on 14 df with p = 0.516) re-run models with REML = FALSE and use `LLchisq(sem.prot)`
